build_note: Build the trusted capacity, stockpiles and redundancy at home, where the country already holds an established position.
gate_note: The gate stays open to allied technology, equipment and investment that speed the repair.

build_note: Build trusted capacity with partners, not at home: compacts, offtake agreements, co-investment and shared stockpiles with allied producers.
gate_note: The gate stays open to those partners' products, investment and equipment, and trusted-source rules recognise allied suppliers.

build_note: Repair the vulnerability by qualifying several trusted suppliers abroad and holding stockpiles, not by building a domestic replica.
gate_note: The gate stays open to every trusted producer; the restriction applies only to the coercive supplier on the fenced node.

build_note: No source holds enough trusted supply to repair the vulnerability alone: create new trusted capacity at home (where a foothold exists or can be built) and with allied partners through co-investment and offtake, and bridge the years until it qualifies with stockpiles.
gate_note: The gate stays open to allied partners' technology, equipment and investment for the capacity not built at home.

build_note: Build at home: production support, finance, workforce and supplier development for the domestic industry, tied to benchmarks.
gate_note: The gate stays open to foreign technology, capital and talent on terms that deepen domestic capability.

build_note: Build the capability jointly with partners (co-investment, joint ventures, offtake, shared R&D); the domestic share is the segment where the country is strongest.
gate_note: The gate stays open to the partners' investment, equipment and engineers, with conditions that favour capability transfer.

build_note: Build a specialised niche in global value chains, the segment where the country is strongest, and source the rest competitively.
gate_note: The gate stays wide for inputs and equipment from a diversified global base.

build_note: Build at home where the base is established and with allied partners for the rest, through co-investment and offtake.
gate_note: The gate stays open to allied partners' investment and equipment, with conditions that favour capability transfer.

build_note: Domestic producers compete on equal terms; no posture-specific production support.
gate_note: Domestic and imported supply compete on equal terms.

build_note: Diversify toward trusted partners through offtake and standards recognition, not production subsidies.
gate_note: The gate stays wide open; allied sourcing is a diversification tool, not an exclusion of other lawful suppliers.

build_note: Supply comes from a diversified global base; the build is enabling infrastructure, not production.
gate_note: The gate stays wide open to a broad supplier base.

build_note: Deployment draws on domestic, allied and global supply on equal terms.
gate_note: The gate stays wide open to all lawful suppliers on equal terms.
